open_points.subject: Runtime delivery of configurable use-case settings
open_points.text: “The settings handed here reach only the store and the transport guard: the inner application and the use cases receive no `RuntimeSettings` and use the `config.*` constants (the staff session lifetime among them).” contradicts A30, where session TTLs and other values are runtime knobs whose deployment values may differ and environment values are read once into `RuntimeSettings`.
open_points.question: How do staff/viewer session TTLs and other use-case runtime knobs reach the operations that use them when `RuntimeSettings` is passed only to the store and transport guard?
options: Pass the relevant runtime settings through application construction to the use cases.
Make these values fixed source constants and cease treating them as deployment runtime knobs.
Install the loaded values into process-global configuration read by use cases.
open_points.default_guess: Pass an immutable settings/config dependency to the operations that need runtime knobs.

witness.initial: A deployment sets the staff-session TTL to 1 hour instead of the 12-hour default.
events: The deployment calls `load_runtime_settings`, which returns a staff-session TTL of 1 hour.
The deployment calls `create_runtime_app` with those settings.
A staff member successfully logs in.
outcomes: Following A30, the issued session expires one hour after login.
Following `create_runtime_app`, the settings never reach `staff_identity`, which uses the source `config.*` value and issues a 12-hour session.
witness.observer: The staff member and any client inspecting `StaffSessionGrant.expires_at`.

open_points.subject: Repeated `/api` prefix routing
open_points.text: “the inner application mounted at `/api` and then at `/`” together with “a path that repeats the prefix (`/api/api/…`) reaches the same route” and `api.create_app` binding every route row exactly once.
open_points.question: What route, if any, handles `/api/api/...` after the first `/api` mount strips only one prefix?
options: Only `/route` and `/api/route` work; `/api/api/route` is not found.
The runtime repeatedly strips `/api` prefixes before routing.
The inner application also registers `/api/...` aliases, despite the exactly-once route-binding statement.
open_points.default_guess: Support the root and single-`/api` forms only; return 404 for a repeated prefix.

witness.initial: The service is running on a trusted host, and the viewer-entry route is registered once in the inner application.
events: A browser sends `POST /api/api/auth/viewer/enter` with a well-formed body containing an invalid access code.
outcomes: The repeated-prefix sentence says the request reaches viewer entry and returns the concealed authentication failure, 401.
With the stated mounts, the `/api` mount consumes one prefix, the inner application receives `/api/auth/viewer/enter`, finds no second registration, and returns 404.

open_points.subject: Accepted representation of `expires_at`
open_points.text: “Any expiry is accepted and stored as supplied, a past one included, never converted” conflicts with A28: “Persisted timestamps are UTC, stored as offset-naive datetimes” and “an offset-aware persisted timestamp ... [is] forbidden.”
open_points.question: Must an offset-aware `expires_at` be rejected, converted to UTC-naive, or persisted unchanged?
options: Reject offset-aware values and accept only UTC-naive datetimes.
Convert an offset-aware instant to UTC-naive before persistence.
Persist the supplied offset-aware value unchanged.
open_points.default_guess: Require a UTC-naive value and reject an offset-aware value as invalid input.

witness.initial: An active service principal exists, and an administrator is authorized to issue its credential.
events: The administrator requests a credential with `expires_at` equal to an offset-aware future datetime such as `2026-11-07T12:00:00+02:00`.
outcomes: Following “any expiry” and “stored as supplied,” the credential is created with an offset-aware persisted timestamp.
Following A28, the request is rejected or the value is converted because an offset-aware persisted timestamp is forbidden.
witness.observer: The administrator, and later code reading the persisted credential.

open_points.subject: Concurrent key-version allocation
open_points.text: “the new `ServiceCredential` with the next `key_version`” and “Writes one `ServiceCredential` and one `AuditRecord`” do not specify the outcome when two issuances concurrently calculate the next version.
open_points.question: When two authorized issuances overlap for the same principal, must both succeed with distinct consecutive key versions, or may one fail with a persistence conflict?
options: Serialize allocation so both succeed with distinct consecutive versions.
Allow one issuance to fail with `PersistenceError` on the unique key-version constraint.
Retry the losing allocation after observing the committed version.
open_points.default_guess: Allocate the version under a serialized write transaction so both successful calls receive distinct versions.

witness.initial: An active principal has latest `key_version` 4 and no version 5 credential.
events: Administrator A starts issuing a credential and reads 4 as the latest version.
Before A commits, administrator B starts issuing another credential for the same principal.
A commits its credential as version 5.
outcomes: A serialized implementation makes B observe version 5 and successfully creates version 6 with its audit.
A read-then-insert implementation makes B attempt version 5 and fail with a persistence error, creating no credential or audit.
witness.observer: Administrator B and operators examining the credential/audit records.

open_points.subject: Concurrent creation of the one manual budget
open_points.text: “Return the project's one manual budget version, creating it empty when absent” and “Writes one `BudgetVersion` and one `AuditRecord` when none exists” do not define the losing call when two calls concurrently observe absence.
open_points.question: Must concurrent first calls both succeed and return the same newly created version, or may one fail at the single-manual-version constraint?
options: Serialize or reload after the uniqueness race so both calls return the same version and only one creation audit exists.
Allow the losing call to raise `PersistenceError`.
Retry the entire losing operation until it reads the winner.
open_points.default_guess: Treat concurrent creation as ensure semantics: one call creates and audits, and every concurrent caller returns that same version.

witness.initial: An active project has no manual budget version, and two staff actors hold valid authorized contexts.
events: Staff A calls `ensure_manual_budget` and observes no manual version.
Before A commits, staff B calls `ensure_manual_budget` and also observes none.
A commits the new empty version and its creation audit.
outcomes: An atomic ensure implementation returns the same version successfully to both callers and writes one creation audit.
A plain check-then-insert implementation makes B violate the one-manual-version constraint and receive `PersistenceError`.
witness.observer: Staff B and clients retrying the ensure operation.
